title: NANSEN Dependency Manifest
description: Schema for dependencies.nansen.json files that declare dependencies for NANSEN core and modules.

_schema_id.description: Canonical URI of the schema that validates this manifest. Used for runtime type-checking by MATLAB and Python.

scope.description: Whether this manifest belongs to core NANSEN or a module.

scopeId.description: Unique identifier for the scope. 'core' for core NANSEN, or a dot-separated module package name (e.g. 'nansen.module.ophys.twophoton').

dependencyType.description: Whether this is a MathWorks product or a community toolbox.

requirementLevel.description: 'required' means NANSEN or the module will not work without it. 'optional' means only specific workflows need it.

scope.description: Overrides the manifest-level scope for this entry. Use 'workflow' for dependencies that belong to a specific workflow within a module. If omitted, inherits from the manifest.

scopeId.description: Overrides the manifest-level scopeId for this entry. Use a workflow-specific identifier like 'nansen.module.ophys.twophoton.workflow.suite2p'. If omitted, inherits from the manifest.

source.description: Install URI for community toolboxes. Supports 'fex://' for FileExchange and 'https://github.com/...' for GitHub. Used to generate requirements.txt.

docsSource.description: URL pointing to installation or usage documentation.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what the dependency provides.

reason.description: Why this dependency is needed. Shown to users for optional dependencies.

workflowNotes.description: Extra context shown when scope is 'workflow'. Explains which workflow requires this dependency.

setupHook.description: Callable to invoke once after installation (e.g. a MATLAB function name or Python entry point). Run during nansen_install or equivalent.

startupHook.description: Callable to invoke on NANSEN startup after the dependency is installed and registered.

installCheck.description: Symbol name used to verify the dependency is installed (e.g. a function, class, or module name). Checked via language-appropriate introspection.

versionConstraint.description: Version requirement string. Reserved for future use.
